Why I chose Flutter over React Native in 2026:

• Single codebase → Android + iOS (not "sort of" — actually)
• Hot reload is faster than RN
• Dart is simpler than JavaScript for mobile
• Widget system is more predictable than JSX + native bridges
• Google is all-in (Gemini, Antigravity, Genkit Dart)

The tradeoff: smaller community, fewer third-party packages.
Worth it for solo devs who want ONE codebase that actually works on both platforms.

📌 One codebase, eats every platform for breakfast: Write it once, package it up for iOS, Android, Web, even Windows and Mac desktop. One person can rival a whole dev team, efficiency skyrockets several times over—it's the no-brainer time-saver that indie devs can't pass up.

📌 Millisecond tweaks, no more compile hell: The killer feature is "Hot Reload." Tweak your code, hit save, and the phone UI updates in under a second—no more agonizing minutes of build waits. Coding feels as breezy as sketching!

💬 One person turns into a full-on army—it's an absolute blast for making money or building products, and designer pals, you can't miss this! 👇

I’ve actually been working on this since the o1 era, lol. That was when I first learned that something called Flutter even existed. I explained my requirements—or more like my preferences—and got recommendations for different technologies, and Flutter seemed like the best fit.

It offers a beautiful UI, solid performance (close to native), and the ability to deploy to multiple platforms from a single codebase. If you include web, that’s basically six platforms you can target all at once. And features like hot reload were a huge plus too.

You know what’s funny? o1 and o1-mini were actually really good at writing code. The core structure of this app is still based on what o1 and o1-mini generated back then. Even today’s state-of-the-art models evaluate that code as solid.

o1 was a really great model.
